### FINDING 1 — lem-the-order-topology-on-an-ordinal — Remark falsely classifies the clopen basic sets
LOCATION: Remarks, line 102
QUOTE: "the sets $(\alpha,\beta]$ are exactly the basic sets that stay clopen"
DEFECT: The word “exactly” is false. The basis also contains clopen initial segments that are not of this form.
EVIDENCE: For the ordinal 1, the set [0,0] is the whole one-point space and is a clopen member of the stated basis. The only possible set of the displayed half-open form is (0,0], which is empty.
SEVERITY: fatal
MINIMAL REPAIR: Replace “are exactly the basic sets that stay clopen” with “are convenient basic sets that are always clopen”.

### FINDING 2 — thm-the-long-line-is-countably-compact-and-not-compact — title omits the choice hypothesis for non-Lindelöfness
LOCATION: Frontmatter title, line 4; compare Statement and choice ledger, lines 49–59
QUOTE: "Every closed initial segment of the long ray is compact; the long ray is countably compact, assuming countable choice; and it is not compact and not Lindel\\\"of"
DEFECT: The punctuation confines the countable-choice qualifier to countable compactness, leaving non-Lindelöfness unqualified. The Statement and proof establish non-Lindelöfness only under countable choice.
EVIDENCE: The item states verbatim, “R is not Lindelöf, assuming the Axiom of Countable Choice,” followed by “Claims 1 and 3 are theorems of ZF. Claims 2 and 4 spend countable choice.”
SEVERITY: fatal
MINIMAL REPAIR: "Every closed initial segment of the long ray is compact; the long ray is not compact; and, assuming countable choice, it is countably compact and not Lindelöf"

### FINDING 3 — thm-quasicomponents-equal-components-in-a-compact-hausdorff-space — final Remark misstates total and local connectedness
LOCATION: Remarks, line 105
QUOTE: "nothing says $X$ is totally disconnected when its components are singletons in some other sense; openness of the components is local connectedness, a separate hypothesis"
DEFECT: Singleton connected components are exactly the library’s definition of total disconnectedness. Moreover, openness of the components of the whole space is strictly weaker than local connectedness, not equivalent to it.
EVIDENCE: The on-disk definition says that a space is totally disconnected when every connected component is a singleton. The later characterization states that local connectedness requires every component of every open subspace to be open, and its Remark says verbatim: “Openness of the components of $X$ alone is strictly weaker.” Explicitly, the closed topologist’s sine curve is compact, Hausdorff, connected and not locally connected; its sole component is the whole space and is therefore open.
SEVERITY: fatal
MINIMAL REPAIR: "Nothing above says the components are open. If all components are singletons, then X is totally disconnected by definition. Local connectedness is a separate sufficient hypothesis that makes components open, but open components alone do not imply local connectedness."
